Python package installs work again on Docker and Podman. The default images can also read and write Excel files.

## Package installs on Docker and Podman

In 0.1.10, every `coala_python_executor` call that listed `packages` failed on Docker and Podman. The install step exited 127 with `exec: "(uv": executable file not found in $PATH`.

The uv-to-pip retry added in 0.1.10 made the install command a shell compound: `(uv pip install ... || (echo ... >&2; python -m pip install ...))`. The Docker SDK splits a string command on whitespace and runs the first word, so `(uv` ran as a program. Commands with conda packages failed the same way. Singularity, Apptainer, and xcrunner were not affected, because they already ran string commands through a shell.

The Docker and Podman manager now runs a string command with `/bin/sh -c`, as the other engines do. The uv-to-pip retry is kept. R package installs were not affected.

## Excel support in the default images

The Python image now includes `openpyxl` (read and write `.xlsx`) and `xlrd` (read `.xls`), so `pandas.read_excel` and `DataFrame.to_excel` work without an install step. The R image now includes `readxl` (read `.xlsx` and `.xls`) and `writexl` (write `.xlsx`). Requests for these packages are skipped on the default images. The new images publish with the `v0.1.11` tag.
